findings.title: Active UART pull guidance states the absolute threshold without the stricter operating condition

evidence.observation: Active UART summaries use pulls-disabled-above4V while allowing0..5V endpoints. Table112 operating conditions require pulls disabled whenever VIN exceeds the relevant supply+0.3V. At3.3V this is3.6V (3.57V at3.27V), leaving3.6..4.0V outside the stated operating condition if a reader treats4V as the configuration threshold. Example3.8V is inside the documented0..5V envelope but above3.6V. Native RX paths are J420.4/R4501k/U1.51 and J410.4/R4401k/U1.64, with no external pull or translator.
evidence.severity_basis: Bounded documentation inconsistency, not a demonstrated electrical failure. The separate binding startup obligation already sets direct UART RX to no pulls; the selected radio is3.3V LVTTL and GPS levels remain explicitly unqualified. A true operating requirement should accompany, rather than be inferred from, an absolute stress condition.

findings.fix: State that GPS/radio digital RX pulls remain disabled throughout use, and distinguish the operating relevant-supply+0.3V condition from Table109 absolute limits in current requirements, ordering, pin/qualification text and generated obligations. Regenerate binding provenance if its source/table changes; no MCU pin or circuit change is established as necessary.
